elements.section: Manage urgently:
elements.text: Ensure the safety of yourself, the patient and those around you: ensure security personnel present, call police if needed. They should disarm patient if s/he has a weapon. Assess patient in a room with other staff and ensure exit is not blocked.

elements.section: Manage urgently:
elements.text: Try to verbally calm the patient:

elements.section: Manage urgently:
elements.text: Avoid direct eye contact, sudden movements and approaching patient from behind. Stand at least two arm's lengths away.

elements.section: Manage urgently:
elements.text: Use an honest, non-threatening manner. Avoid talking down to the patient, arguing or commanding him/her to calm down. Use a friendly gesture like offering a drink or food.

elements.section: Manage urgently:
elements.text: Listen to patient, identify his/her feelings and desires and offer choices. Take all threats seriously.

elements.section: Manage urgently:
elements.text: Consider involuntary admission if signs of mental illness and refuses treatment/admission and a danger to self, others, own reputation or financial interest/property 158.

elements.section: Manage urgently:
elements.text: Restrain and/or sedate only if absolutely needed (imminent harm to self/others, disruption of important treatment, damage to environment, verbal attempts to calm patient failed).

elements.section: Manage urgently:
elements.text: If possible, before sedation, assess and manage possible causes of abnormal thoughts or behaviour 36.

elements.section: Manage urgently:
elements.text: If restraints used, document type, duration and site and check restraint sites every 15 minutes. Counsel the family regarding reasons for restraints.

elements.section: Give urgent attention to the aggressive/disruptive patient with any of:
elements.text: Try to avoid IM/IV medication to sedate the aggressive/disruptive patient, especially if > 65 years or substance user.

elements.section: Manage urgently:
elements.text: Ensure emergency trolley and resuscitation equipment available before giving sedation. Will patient accept oral medication?

elements.section: Give urgent attention to the aggressive/disruptive patient with any of:
elements.text: Give diazepam 5mg orally or buccal1 midazolam 7.5-15mg.

elements.section: Manage urgently:
elements.text: Give midazolam 7.5-15mg IM or diazepam 10mg IV over 2 minutes.

elements.section: Give urgent attention to the aggressive/disruptive patient with any of:
elements.text: Give haloperidol 0.5-1mg IM. If haloperidol not available:

elements.section: Manage urgently:
elements.text: If alcohol withdrawal, also give thiamine 200mg IM.

elements.section: Give urgent attention to the aggressive/disruptive patient with any of:
elements.text: Give olanzapine 5-10mg orodispersible/IM. If > 65 years, give 2.5-5mg orodispersible/IM instead.

elements.section: Give urgent attention to the aggressive/disruptive patient with any of:
elements.text: If previous olanzapine intolerance (fever, sweating, muscle rigidity and changes in blood pressure) give midazolam 7.5-15mg IM.

elements.section: Give urgent attention to the aggressive/disruptive patient with any of:
elements.text: Assess response after 30 minutes:

elements.section: Manage urgently:
elements.text: Patient calm

elements.section: Give urgent attention to the aggressive/disruptive patient with any of:
elements.text: If partial response or no response, repeat same dose of medication used above

elements.section: Manage urgently:
elements.text: Monitor and record temperature, BP, respiratory and pulse rate, level of consciousness every 15 minutes for first hour, then every 30 minutes until patient referred, or alert and walking.

elements.section: Manage urgently:
elements.text: Once patient is calmer, reassess for underlying cause if not already done, and manage further 36.

elements.section: Manage urgently:
elements.text: Refer the mentally ill aggressive patient to hospital same day3: document history, and time and dose of medication given. If emergency admission needed without patient consent, fill in MHCA 01 form. If restraints used, complete MHCA 48 form.
AGGRESSIVE/DISRUPTIVE BEHAVIOUR

1Buccal: use IV formulation of midazolam, use syringe to draw up correct dose, remove needle and give midazolam between the cheek and gum. 2Stimulants include: methamphetamines (tik), cocaine (crack), methaqualone (mandrax), cannabis. 3If delay in transport, try to move patient to most calm/quiet area and enlist help of a family member to monitor patient.
